acceptance: `evolve inbox edit <id> --set weight=0.4` rewrites only that field and appends a ledger line (red: usage error)
A deps entry naming no item, or a duplicate id, is refused with exit 1 and leaves the file unchanged
fix: Add `evolve inbox edit <id> --set key=value… [--add key=value] [--remove key=value]` for the curation fields: weight, priority_class, files, deps, connects_to, title, acceptance, and the id of an id-less item named by its path. It validates the result with the checks `inbox add` applies (schema, unique id, deps naming existing items), writes atomically through the lifecycle's item writer, and appends a ledger line. Lifecycle fields (route, routed_*, failure counts) exit 10. Exit 1 for an unknown id or a failed validation, 2 on I/O. Document it in runtime-reference.md's operator commands.
source: console, 2026-09-30, core-function CLI inventory (operator request: a CLI request for each core function)
summary: No verb changes an item. The 2026-09-27 curation stamped ids into five id-less items by hand (inbox inbox-item-identity-one-rule), and every reweight, file-list correction or dependency change is a JSON edit that nothing validates. A typo in deps leaves an item waiting forever, and a malformed file is skipped with only a WARN from batches.
title: Curating an inbox item (weight, files, deps, a missing id) is a hand edit of its JSON plus a PR; add `evolve inbox edit`
